clue.text: Wampum used for buying cannon-fodder?

definitions.meaning: strings of shell beads once used as currency by Native North Americans
read as cash spent on artillery shells, the ammunition a cannon is fed

explanation.surface: A question about Native American bead currency being spent on soldiers sent to die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cannon-fodder' usually means expendable troops, but here it is literally what a cannon eats: shells. Money for buying shells is the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Wampum is bead currency made from seashells, the standard example of this kind of primitive cash.

clue.text: Its purpose in sport is to eliminate passion

definitions.text: Its purpose in sport is to eliminate
definitions.meaning: a qualifying round in athletics or swimming that knocks out the slower competitors
intense feeling, as in the warmth of an argument

explanation.surface: A remark that sport exists to stamp out strong emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary race round is so called in athletics, and the same word names fiery ardour or anger.

clue.text: A roof ventilator not to be missed in Paris

definitions.meaning: a slatted opening in a roof that lets smoke or air out

definitions.text: not to be missed in Paris
definitions.meaning: the great art museum that every visitor to the French capital is told to see

explanation.surface: A roof vent is recommended as a sight for tourists in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A slatted roof vent shares its name with the famous Paris museum, a must-see attraction.

clue.text: Fellow unfitted for work on a tough paper

parts.note: a fellow is a man
someone too sick to work is ill

explanation.surface: A man too sick to work is set to labour on some hard-wearing paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong brown wrapping paper, originally made from Manila hemp, goes by this name.

clue.text: In short the man who toppled the crown!

definitions.text: In short the man who toppled the crown!

parts.words: In short the man who toppled the crown!
parts.note: a nickname, shortened from a first name, for Cromwell, who overthrew Charles I

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a revolutionary who brought down the monarchy, put briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Cromwell, who led the English Parliament against King Charles I, was nicknamed 'Old Noll', a pet form of Oliver; 'In short' points to that shortened name.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar shortening of Oliver, it was the name royalists used for Cromwell, the regicide.

clue.text: Longed for a period of time to study reaction?

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: a reaction moves back the other way, so the study word is turned round

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Someone has wished for some time to study how a substance reacts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reaction' suggests chemistry, but it signals turning the study word round to follow the period of time; 'for' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to pine after it, the same wistful desire.

clue.text: Fought over crude metal racket

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: fought means battled
ore is metal in its crude, unrefined state

explanation.surface: A row broke out over a rough metal tennis racket.
explanation.walkthrough: A battledore is the bat used in the old game battledore and shuttlecock, ancestor of badminton.
explanation.definitionFit: The bat in the old shuttlecock game was a small stringed or parchment-faced racket.

clue.text: A vehicle drawn up in accordance with the law

definitions.meaning: any means of transport, a carriage or cart

definitions.text: drawn up in accordance with the law
definitions.meaning: a legal deed transferring property, drafted by a lawyer

explanation.surface: A vehicle is pulled over in line with the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn up' suggests a car pulling up, but it means a document being drafted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a means of transport and a deed transferring ownership of property.

clue.text: Bill returned to a stern old censor

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the bill's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: An account is sent back to a strict official of former times.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder was a Roman censor famed for his severity.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato was the Roman magistrate notorious for strict morals while holding the office of censor.

clue.text: Wild revels of Australian derivation

indicators.note: a derivation is something formed out of another, so these letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Unruly parties said to come from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derivation' signals that the letters of AUSTRALIAN are rearranged; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman winter festival gave its name to any riotous merrymaking or orgy.

clue.text: Don's finest port?

parts.note: not a university fellow's best wine but the leading port city on the river Don in Russia

explanation.surface: A question about which port wine a university lecturer would rate highest.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'don' is an Oxford or Cambridge lecturer and port is a fortified wine, a common pairing; here the Don is the Russian river and the port is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostov-on-Don is the major port city on that Russian river near the Sea of Azov.

clue.text: Length of cloth once soaked in some turbid white wine

indicators.note: something soaked in liquid sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
turbid means stirred up and cloudy, so the letters of the word some are churned

parts.note: an ell was an old measure of cloth, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: An old measure of fabric is drenched in muddy wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbid' looks like a description of the wine but stirs up the letters of 'some' to MOSE; 'soaked in' then puts the old cloth measure inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine from the valley of the river of that name in Germany is typically a light dry white.

clue.text: Uniformly applied emergency ruling?

parts.note: read as rule imposed by people in uniform, the army, during a crisis

explanation.surface: A question about a crisis regulation enforced evenly across the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniformly' seems to mean consistently, but it means by those in uniform: soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Military government imposed in an emergency, suspending ordinary civil rule.

clue.text: The going price for travel

parts.note: read as the cost of a ticket for the outward going only, with no return

explanation.surface: The current market rate for a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The going price' looks like the usual rate, but 'going' means one-way, outward only.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket covering a journey in one direction only, without the return trip.

clue.text: French spa whose turnover is not affected

indicators.note: a turnover flips something round, so the word for not affected is read backwards

parts.note: naive means artless, without affectation

explanation.surface: A French resort whose business takes no hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like trade but reverses NAIVE; 'whose' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Évian-les-Bains is a spa town on Lake Geneva famous for its mineral water.

clue.text: The ministerial office 6 reconstituted

indicators.note: reconstituted means put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: points to the answer at 6-down, a word meaning longed

explanation.surface: A government department is rebuilt, as entry six says.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' stands for the answer to 6-down, whose letters 'reconstituted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean's office or residence is the post held by a cleric of that rank, a minister of the church.

clue.text: I'd returned with spirit to prepare a defensive position

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so I'd is read backwards

parts.note: the letters of I'd without the apostrophe
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone came back with a drink to brace themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers entrench, excavating a trench to hold ground against attack.

clue.text: Rejected eggs I'd keep away from

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for eggs is read backwards

parts.note: ova are eggs
the letters of I'd without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone shuns eggs they have turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun something is to steer clear of it.

clue.text: Mysterious Old Norse literary character

parts.note: a letter of the ancient Germanic alphabet, thought to carry magic

explanation.surface: A shadowy figure from a Viking saga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literary character' suggests a person in a story, but it is a written letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of the old Scandinavian futhark alphabet, often credited with magical meaning.

clue.text: Blue fluff?

explanation.surface: A two-word puzzle pairing a colour with fuzz.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means dejected and also the soft under-feathers of a bird.

clue.text: Type of grass that could cause a stampede

definitions.meaning: a genus of grasses, including millet
sudden terror that sends a herd or crowd running

explanation.surface: Grass that might set a herd running.
explanation.definitionFit: Panicum is a grass genus, and the word also means a sudden overwhelming fright.

clue.text: They are said to get help from a superior power

definitions.text: They are said to get help from a superior power

parts.words: They are said to get help from a superior power
parts.note: requests spoken to God, a higher power, asking for aid

explanation.surface: People reputed to receive assistance from someone above them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are said' looks like 'are reputed', but these things are literally spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Petitions offered to God are recited aloud in hope of divine help.

clue.text: Twin rhyme upheld by English friend of Erasmus

indicators.note: held by means gripped inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: John Colet, the English scholar and Dean of St Paul's, was a close friend of Erasmus
taken as written, the first part of the word upheld

explanation.surface: A matched pair of rhyming lines is supported by an English companion of the Dutch scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheld' reads as one word but splits: 'up' is the inner piece and 'held by' the container signal, around the scholar's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Two consecutive verse lines that rhyme form a pair, the twin rhyme of the clue.

clue.text: Act of unkindness that can make one feel queasy?

definitions.meaning: a bad deed done to someone

definitions.text: that can make one feel queasy?
definitions.meaning: read as a sick spell, a bout of illness

explanation.surface: A nasty deed that might make someone feel sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmful deed, the opposite of a good turn; read literally, a sickly spell.

clue.text: Quite out of place in any event of course

definitions.meaning: in racing, a horse finishing unplaced in a race is said to be so

explanation.surface: Something is entirely inappropriate whatever happens, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in any event of course' reads as 'anyway, naturally', but means in any race on a racecourse; 'out of place' is unplaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse finishing far behind the placed runners is said to have come in so, unplaced and at no location.

clue.text: Kind of robbery most likely to occur during rush hours

definitions.meaning: an armed raid on a bank or vehicle

definitions.text: most likely to occur during rush hours

explanation.surface: A type of theft that happens mostly at the busiest commuting times.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an armed robbery and a traffic delay.

clue.text: Ireland's flow of capital

parts.note: not money moving but the river flowing through Dublin, Ireland's capital

explanation.surface: Money moving through the Irish economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flow of capital' sounds financial, but it is the river of the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The river that runs through the middle of Dublin.

clue.text: See ducks going over a Scandinavian capital

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece going over another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, written O, so ducks are OS
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: A sighting of ducks flying over a city in northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Norway.

clue.text: A catch made of tin and silver

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A fastening made of two metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden drawback or difficulty is a catch.

clue.text: An idol's eye transformed? No problem!

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: here the S counts as a letter

explanation.surface: A question about a statue's eye being changed, then reassurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easily accomplished presents no difficulty.

clue.text: Port that's a credit to the East

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts; that the answer also runs through the letters of 'a credit' is a coincidence of this charade
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A harbour that brings honour to the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a credit to' suggests praise; 'to' is a link word. Acre is an ancient port in northern Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is a historic harbour town on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Feature of paper giving play reviews?

definitions.text: Feature of paper giving play reviews?

parts.words: Feature of paper giving play reviews?
parts.note: not theatre criticism but reports on games and matches in a newspaper section

explanation.surface: A newspaper section reviewing stage productions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests drama, but here it is sporting play.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper section covering games and athletics reports on the play in matches.
